title: Constant acceleration: position, velocity, acceleration
caption: A body with $v_0=2\,\mathrm{m/s}$ and $a=1.5\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$. The slope of the $x$-$t$ curve is $v$, the slope of the $v$-$t$ line is $a$ and the area under the $v$-$t$ line is the displacement.

title: Projectile motion: trajectories for five launch angles
caption: Launch speed $20\,\mathrm{m/s}$, no air resistance. Complementary angles ($15^\circ$ and $75^\circ$, $30^\circ$ and $60^\circ$) give the same range; the maximum range is at $45^\circ$.

title: Free fall with and without air resistance
caption: Linear drag $F=-bv$ with terminal speed $30\,\mathrm{m/s}$: the speed approaches $v_t$ exponentially with time constant $\tau=v_t/g$, while without drag it grows without limit.

title: Reading motion graphs: a(t), v(t) and x(t) of one trip
caption: Acceleration $+2\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$ for $3\,\mathrm{s}$, then $0$ for $3\,\mathrm{s}$, then $-1.5\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$ for $4\,\mathrm{s}$. The area under $a$-$t$ is the change of $v$; the area under $v$-$t$ is the change of $x$; the body stops at $t=10\,\mathrm{s}$ after $39\,\mathrm{m}$.

title: Adding and subtracting vectors by components
caption: $\vec A=(3,4)$ and $\vec B=(-1,2)$: add or subtract component by component; the magnitude of the sum is $\sqrt{40}=6.32$, not $|A|+|B|=7.24$.

title: Acceleration down an incline against the angle
caption: $a=g(\sin\theta-\mu\cos\theta)$ once $\tan\theta>\mu$; below that angle friction holds the block. At $90^\circ$ every curve reaches $g$ (free fall).

title: Atwood machine: acceleration and tension against the mass ratio
caption: $m_1=1\,\mathrm{kg}$ and $m_2=r\,m_1$. For $r\to\infty$ the acceleration approaches $g$ and the tension approaches $2m_1g$; for $r=1$ nothing moves and $T=m_1g$.

title: Static and kinetic friction against the applied force
caption: A $10\,\mathrm{kg}$ crate ($\mu_s=0.5$, $\mu_k=0.3$): friction equals the applied force until $\mu_smg=49\,\mathrm{N}$, then drops to $\mu_kmg=29.4\,\mathrm{N}$ and the crate accelerates.

title: Hooke's law: single springs, springs in parallel and in series
caption: $k_1=200\,\mathrm{N/m}$, $k_2=300\,\mathrm{N/m}$. In parallel the constants add ($500$); in series the compliances add, so the combination is softer than either spring ($120$).

title: Apparent weight in an elevator
caption: A $60\,\mathrm{kg}$ passenger: $+1.5\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$ for $2\,\mathrm{s}$, cruise, then $-1.5\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$ for $2\,\mathrm{s}$. The scale reads $N=m(g+a)$: more than $mg$ while speeding up, exactly $mg$ at constant speed, less while slowing down.

title: Work as the area under the force-position graph
caption: A force that rises to $3\,\mathrm{N}$ over the first $2\,\mathrm{m}$, stays constant to $4\,\mathrm{m}$ and falls to zero at $6\,\mathrm{m}$ does $3+6+3=12\,\mathrm{J}$ of work. The right panel is the running total $W(x)$.

title: A potential-energy curve: turning points and kinetic energy
caption: For $U(x)=x^4/4-x^2$ (joules) and total energy $E=-0.6\,\mathrm{J}$ the particle can only be where $U\le E$; the kinetic energy $K=E-U$ is the gap between the line and the curve. The force is minus the slope of $U$.

title: One-dimensional collisions against the mass ratio
caption: $m_1=1\,\mathrm{kg}$ at $4\,\mathrm{m/s}$ hits $m_2=r\,m_1$ at rest. Elastic: $m_1$ stops at $r=1$ and bounces back for $r>1$. Perfectly inelastic: the common speed is $u/(1+r)$ and the fraction $r/(1+r)$ of the kinetic energy is lost.

title: Impulse of a collision force
caption: A half-sine force pulse of peak $600\,\mathrm{N}$ lasting $10\,\mathrm{ms}$ gives an impulse $2F_0T/\pi=3.82\,\mathrm{N\,s}$; on a $0.15\,\mathrm{kg}$ ball that is a velocity change of $25.5\,\mathrm{m/s}$.

title: Power needed by a car against its speed
caption: Resistance $F=200+0.4v^2$ (newtons). The power needed, $P=Fv$, grows like $v^3$ at high speed; with a $60\,\mathrm{kW}$ engine the top speed is where the curve crosses $60\,\mathrm{kW}$.

title: Centripetal force against speed and radius
caption: A $1000\,\mathrm{kg}$ car on a circular path: $F=mv^2/r$ grows with the square of the speed and falls with the radius. Friction (or banking) must supply it, which is why sharp bends are taken slowly.

title: Ideal speed on a banked curve
caption: On a frictionless banked bend the normal force alone supplies the centripetal force: $\tan\theta=v^2/(rg)$. The ideal speed grows with the bank angle and with the radius.

title: Rotation with constant angular acceleration
caption: $\alpha=2\,\mathrm{rad/s^2}$, $\omega_0=1\,\mathrm{rad/s}$, point at $r=0.30\,\mathrm{m}$. The tangential speed $v=\omega r$ grows linearly; the centripetal acceleration $\omega^2r$ grows quadratically; the tangential acceleration $\alpha r$ is constant.

title: Moment of inertia and the rolling race
caption: $I=\beta MR^2$ with $\beta=1$ (hoop), $\tfrac23$ (hollow sphere), $\tfrac12$ (cylinder), $\tfrac25$ (solid sphere). Rolling down a $30^\circ$ incline, $a=g\sin\theta/(1+\beta)$: the smaller $\beta$, the faster; a frictionless sliding block beats them all.

title: Conservation of angular momentum: the spinning skater
caption: With no external torque $L=I\omega$ stays constant ($8\,\mathrm{kg\,m^2/s}$). Pulling the arms in lowers $I$ from $4$ to $1\,\mathrm{kg\,m^2}$: $\omega$ rises from $2$ to $8\,\mathrm{rad/s}$ and the kinetic energy from $8$ to $32\,\mathrm{J}$ (the skater does the work).

title: Heating curve of 1 kg of water from ice at −20 °C to steam at 120 °C
caption: Slopes are set by the specific heats (ice $2090$, water $4186$, steam $2010\,\mathrm{J/kg\,K}$); the plateaus are the latent heats of fusion ($334\,\mathrm{kJ}$) and vaporisation ($2256\,\mathrm{kJ}$). Total heat: $3090.6\,\mathrm{kJ}$.
formula: Q=mc\,\Delta T\ \ (\text{no phase change}),\qquad Q=mL\ \ (\text{phase change})

title: Thermal expansion of 1 m rods
caption: $\Delta L=\alpha L\,\Delta T$: for the same temperature rise aluminium ($23\times10^{-6}\,\mathrm{K^{-1}}$) grows almost twice as much as steel ($12\times10^{-6}$), copper ($17\times10^{-6}$) and Pyrex glass ($3.2\times10^{-6}$) far less.
formula: \Delta L=\alpha L\,\Delta T,\qquad \Delta A\approx2\alpha A\,\Delta T,\qquad \Delta V\approx3\alpha V\,\Delta T

title: Calorimetry: final temperature of a mixture
caption: Hot liquid at $80^\circ\mathrm{C}$ poured into cold water at $20^\circ\mathrm{C}$. With the same specific heat the temperature is a mass-weighted average; oil ($c=2000\,\mathrm{J/kg\,K}$) gives up less heat per kilogram, so the mixture stays cooler.

title: Work on a p-V diagram: isothermal and isobaric expansion
caption: $0.10\,\mathrm{mol}$ of ideal gas at $300\,\mathrm{K}$ expands from $2\,\mathrm{L}$ to $6\,\mathrm{L}$. The work is the area under the path: $nRT\ln3=274\,\mathrm{J}$ along the isotherm, $p_1\Delta V=499\,\mathrm{J}$ at constant pressure.
formula: W=\int p\,dV,\qquad W_{\rm iso}=nRT\ln\frac{V_2}{V_1},\qquad W_{\rm isobar}=p\,\Delta V

title: Maxwell speed distribution of nitrogen
caption: $N_2$ ($M=28\,\mathrm{g/mol}$) at $300\,\mathrm{K}$ and $600\,\mathrm{K}$. The most probable speed is below the mean, which is below the rms speed: $v_p<v_{\rm avg}<v_{\rm rms}$. Raising $T$ shifts and flattens the curve; the area stays $1$.
formula: f(v)=4\pi\left(\frac{M}{2\pi RT}\right)^{3/2}v^2e^{-Mv^2/2RT},\quad v_p=\sqrt{\tfrac{2RT}{M}},\ v_{\rm avg}=\sqrt{\tfrac{8RT}{\pi M}},\ v_{\rm rms}=\sqrt{\tfrac{3RT}{M}}

title: Isotherms and an adiabat of an ideal gas
caption: One mole of a monatomic gas ($\gamma=5/3$). Along an isotherm $pV$ is constant; along an adiabat $pV^\gamma$ is constant, so the adiabat is steeper: at the crossing point its slope is $\gamma$ times the slope of the isotherm.

title: Molar heat capacities and the number of degrees of freedom
caption: $C_V=\tfrac f2R$ and $C_p=C_V+R$: monatomic gases ($f=3$) have $\gamma=5/3$, diatomic gases at room temperature ($f=5$) $\gamma=7/5$, polyatomic gases ($f=6$) $\gamma=4/3$.

title: Mean free path of nitrogen against pressure
caption: $\lambda=kT/(\sqrt2\,\pi d^2p)$ with $d=3.7\times10^{-10}\,\mathrm{m}$ at $300\,\mathrm{K}$: inversely proportional to the pressure (slope $-1$ on log-log axes), about $67\,\mathrm{nm}$ at one atmosphere and millimetres in a rough vacuum.

title: Efficiency of a Carnot engine
caption: $\eta=1-T_c/T_h$ depends only on the two reservoir temperatures: it falls linearly with $T_c/T_h$, and for $T_c=300\,\mathrm{K}$ it rises with $T_h$ but can never reach $1$. For $500\,\mathrm{K}$ and $300\,\mathrm{K}$ it is $40\,\%$.

title: The Carnot cycle on a p-V diagram
caption: One mole of a monatomic gas between $500\,\mathrm{K}$ and $300\,\mathrm{K}$: isothermal expansion A→B (heat $Q_h$ in), adiabatic expansion B→C, isothermal compression C→D (heat $Q_c$ out), adiabatic compression D→A. The enclosed area is the work, and $W/Q_h=1-T_c/T_h=0.40$.

title: Entropy change when water is heated
caption: Heating $1\,\mathrm{kg}$ of water from $280$ to $360\,\mathrm{K}$: $\Delta S=mc\ln(T_2/T_1)=1052\,\mathrm{J/K}$. On the $T$-$S$ diagram the area under the curve is the heat absorbed, $mc\,\Delta T=335\,\mathrm{kJ}$.

title: Refrigerator and heat-pump coefficients of performance
caption: For a Carnot refrigerator $K=T_c/(T_h-T_c)$ and for a heat pump $K=T_h/(T_h-T_c)=K_{\rm fridge}+1$ (room at $T_h=300\,\mathrm{K}$). Both blow up as $T_c\to T_h$: moving heat across a small temperature difference is cheap.
